examples.en: The club dismissed the manager because of poor results.

examples.ko: 회사는 문제를 일으킨 임원을 경질하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to remove the executive who caused the problem.
Demands to dismiss the minister kept coming up.

examples.ko: 팀이 감독을 경질해도 성적이 금방 오르지는 않아요.
examples.en: Even if a team replaces its manager, results don't improve right away.

examples.ko: 왜 갑자기 코치를 경질했는지 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows why they suddenly replaced the coach.
The CEO announced that he would replace the person in charge.

explain: '누가 누구를 경질하다' 형태로 쓰고, 구단·회사·정부처럼 윗선이 주어, 바뀌는 사람이 목적어예요. '해임하다'와 비슷하고 스포츠 기사에서 감독 이야기에도 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '자르다'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The minister was dismissed after a controversy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경질하다'의 피동형으로, 바뀌는 사람을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of 경질하다, used with the person being replaced as the subject.

phrases.en: The company dismissed the president.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경질하다'와 비슷한데 회사나 기관의 일반적인 공식 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 경질하다, but a general formal expression for companies and organizations.

phrases.example: 성적이 나쁘다고 감독을 자르자는 말이 나와요.
phrases.en: People are saying the coach should be fired for poor results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '경질하다'를 거칠고 쉽게 바꿔 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A rough, easy way to say 경질하다 in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It is used in the pattern 'A replaces B', where the higher-ups such as a club, company or government are the subject and the person removed is the object. It is similar to '해임하다' and is also used in sports articles about managers. In everyday talk, people sometimes say '자르다' instead.

examples.ko: 고사장에 들어갈 때 수험표를 꼭 보여 주세요.
examples.en: Please be sure to show your exam admission ticket when entering the exam hall.

examples.ko: 고사장이 집에서 너무 멀어서 일찍 출발했어요.
examples.en: The exam site was so far from home that I left early.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 고사장을 미리 확인해 두었어요.
examples.en: I checked the exam site in advance the day before the test.
My friends cheered me on in front of the exam hall.
You must keep your phone turned off in the exam hall.
The exam site is decided differently by each school.

explain: 큰 시험을 볼 때 시험을 치르는 장소를 가리켜요. '시험장'이라고도 하고, 수능이나 자격시험 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 보통 '고사장 안내', '고사장 입실'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Please check the exam site's location in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고사장'과 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때는 '시험장'이 조금 더 쉽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 고사장; 시험장 sounds a bit more everyday.

phrases.example: 고사장 입실은 여덟 시 십 분까지예요.
phrases.en: Entry to the exam room is until 8:10.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 안내문에서 시간을 알릴 때 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in exam notices when giving the time to enter.

phrases.en: I got the exam site information by text message.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 전에 장소와 방법을 알려 주는 안내를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the information about where and how to take the exam.

explain_en: It means the place where a big exam is taken. People also say '시험장', and it appears often in notices for the CSAT or certification exams. It is typically used as '고사장 안내' (site guide) or '고사장 입실' (entering the hall).

t90.ax: My friends cheered me on in front of the exam hall.

en: to attack; to tackle a target

examples.ko: 이 게임의 어려운 단계를 공략하는 방법을 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I looked up how to beat the hard stage of this game.

examples.ko: 새 가게는 젊은 손님을 공략해서 메뉴를 바꿨어요.
examples.en: The new shop changed its menu to target young customers.
The other team went after our weak point.

examples.ko: 시험 공부는 어려운 문제부터 공략해 보세요.
examples.en: When studying for the test, try tackling the hard problems first.

examples.ko: 해외 시장을 공략하기 위해 영어 홈페이지를 만들었어요.
examples.en: We made an English website to break into overseas markets.

examples.ko: 보스를 공략하려면 먼저 아이템을 모아야 해요.
examples.en: To beat the boss, you first need to collect items.

explain: 원래는 적을 공격해서 빼앗는다는 뜻인데, 요즘은 게임 '공략', 시장 '공략'처럼 목표를 정하고 방법을 짜서 해낼 때 많이 써요. '공략집', '공략법' 같은 명사도 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: This boss is easy if you look at a walkthrough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임이나 시험을 해내는 방법을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the method of beating a game or a test.

phrases.en: The company is targeting overseas markets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사업에서 새 고객층이나 시장을 목표로 삼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in business for targeting a new customer group or market.

phrases.example: 이번에는 새 방법으로 이 단계를 공략해 볼게요.
phrases.en: This time I'll try to tackle this level with a new method.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'를 붙여 새 방법을 시도한다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 보다 adds the sense of trying a new approach.

explain_en: Strategic approach to a game stage, market or opponent. Its original sense is attacking an enemy to take a position, but today it is used for planning a way to beat a target, as in game walkthroughs or market strategy. Nouns like 공략집 and 공략법 are common too.

t90.ax: The other team went after our weak point.

examples.en: I bought a camera with a good optical lens.
I majored in optics in college.
Optical technology has advanced, so photos are sharp.

examples.ko: 이 현미경은 광학 방식으로 작은 것을 크게 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This microscope magnifies small things with an optical method.
For cameras, optical zoom is important.

examples.ko: 동생은 광학에 관심이 많아서 빛 실험을 좋아해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is into optics and loves experiments with light.

explain: 카메라, 안경, 현미경 이야기에서 자주 들려요. '광학 줌'은 렌즈로 크게 보는 방법이고, '디지털 줌'과 달리 화질이 잘 안 떨어져요. 학교에서는 빛을 배우는 분야 이름으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 이 카메라는 광학 줌이 좋아서 멀리서도 선명하게 찍혀요.
phrases.en: This camera has a good optical zoom, so photos are clear even from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 렌즈로 크게 보는 방법이에요. 디지털 줌보다 화질이 덜 떨어져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Zooming in with the lens itself; image quality drops less than with digital zoom.

phrases.en: Microscopes and telescopes are optical instruments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 렌즈나 거울로 빛을 이용하는 기계를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to devices that use light through lenses or mirrors.

phrases.example: 광학을 공부하면 빛의 성질을 잘 알 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you study optics, you can understand the properties of light well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛을 배우는 학문 분야로 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about optics as an academic field about light.

explain_en: Often heard when talking about cameras, glasses, and microscopes. '광학 줌' (optical zoom) uses the lens and, unlike '디지털 줌' (digital zoom), keeps image quality. In school it is also the name of the field that studies light.

examples.ko: 이 책은 처음 한국어를 배우는 사람을 위한 길라잡이예요.
examples.en: This book is a guide for people learning Korean for the first time.
I planned the route after looking at a travel guide.

examples.ko: 선생님은 우리에게 인생의 길라잡이가 되어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Our teacher became a guide in life for us.
I received a guidebook for new employees.

examples.ko: 좋은 길라잡이 덕분에 산을 안전하게 올랐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a good guide, we climbed the mountain safely.

examples.ko: 이 글을 작은 길라잡이로 삼아 보세요.
examples.en: Try using this text as a small guide.

explain: 길을 안내하는 사람뿐 아니라 입문서나 안내서, 어떤 일의 방향을 알려 주는 사람이나 글에도 써요. 책 제목에 '~ 길라잡이'가 자주 붙어요. 비슷한 말로 '길잡이', '안내자'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 이 책이 제 공부의 길잡이가 되어 줬어요.
phrases.en: This book became a guide for my studies.
phrases.nuance_ko: '길라잡이'와 같은 뜻이고, 더 짧아서 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 길라잡이 but shorter and common in speech.

phrases.en: My senior became a guide for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 누군가에게 방향을 알려 주는 역할을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person plays the role of showing direction to someone.

phrases.en: This app is a guide for learning Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분야 이름 + 길라잡이'는 책이나 서비스 이름으로 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A 'field + 길라잡이' pattern often seen in book or service names.

explain_en: It means not only a person who leads the way but also an introductory book, guidebook, or a person or text that shows the direction of something. '~ 길라잡이' often appears in book titles. Similar words are '길잡이' and '안내자'.

t90.ax: Try using this text as a small guide.

examples.en: I took a logic class at university.
The logic professor gave us a hard problem.
Philosophy students always study logic.
The logic book was too hard, so I gave up.
My younger sibling says math is easier than logic.
I studied all night for the logic exam.

explain: '논리'는 생각이 이어지는 짜임이고, '논리학'은 그것을 공부하는 학문이에요. 철학, 수학과 가까워요. '논리적이다'와 헷갈리지 마세요. 발음은 [놀리학]이에요.

phrases.en: The logic class is more fun than I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 배우는 과목으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about it as a school subject.

phrases.en: I want to study logic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학문으로서 배운다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means studying it as an academic field.

phrases.en: That person is a famous logician.
phrases.nuance_ko: 논리학을 연구하는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who studies logic.

explain_en: Logic as an academic subject or field of study, like a university course. '논리' is how thoughts connect, and '논리학' is the field that studies it, close to philosophy and math. Don't mix it up with '논리적이다' (logical). It is pronounced [놀리학].

t90.ax: I took a logic class at university.

examples.en: On the weekend I went to a strawberry farm with my family.

examples.ko: 이 농원에서는 직접 과일을 따 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this farm you can pick the fruit yourself.

examples.ko: 농원 주인이 사과를 한 봉지 더 주셨어요.
examples.en: The farm owner gave me one more bag of apples.
The couple who run the farm appeared on TV.
There is also a small cafe near the farm.
The tangerines from our farm are known for being sweet.

explain: '농장'과 비슷하지만 '○○농원'처럼 체험 장소나 가게 이름에 붙은 모습을 자주 볼 수 있어요. 과일이나 꽃, 채소를 키우는 곳 이야기에 어울려요.

phrases.en: I picked strawberries myself at a strawberry farm.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농원' 앞에 작물 이름을 붙여 어떤 곳인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A crop name before '농원' tells what kind of farm it is.

phrases.en: This weekend I'm going to a farm with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체험이나 나들이로 방문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when visiting for an activity or outing.

phrases.en: My grandfather runs a farm in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농원'과 비슷하지만 일반적으로 농사짓는 곳 전체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '농원' but refers to a farm in general.

explain_en: It is similar to '농장' (farm), but you often see it attached to the names of experience farms and shops, like '○○농원'. It fits places that grow fruit, flowers or vegetables.

t90.ax: There is also a small cafe near the farm.

examples.en: The teacher urges students to read books.
The team leader finished the work while urging the staff on.
The city hall encouraged citizens to recycle.

examples.ko: 코치가 선수들을 큰 소리로 독려하고 있어요.
examples.en: The coach is urging the players on in a loud voice.
I prepared prizes to encourage the children to take part.
My parents urged me on, so I studied until the end.

explain: 그냥 응원하는 '격려하다'와 달리 윗사람이나 책임자가 일이나 공부를 더 열심히 하도록 이끄는 느낌이 있어요. 팀장·코치·기관이 쓸 때가 많고 '참여를 독려하다'처럼 자주 쓰는 짝말이 있어요.

phrases.en: City hall encourages citizens to take part.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 활동에 사람들이 나서도록 이끌 때 쓰는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for urging people to join an event or activity.

phrases.en: My friend encouraged me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 아니어도 쓰고, 마음을 북돋워 주는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for anyone, not just superiors, and feels more about lifting someone's spirits.

phrases.en: Encouraged by my teacher, I prepared for the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 독려를 받는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the person being encouraged is the subject.

explain_en: Leader pushing a group to keep going until the end. Unlike 격려하다, which is simple cheering, 독려하다 feels like a leader pushing people to work or study harder. Team leaders, coaches, and institutions use it often, with a common pairing like 참여를 독려하다.

t90.ax: The teacher urges students to read books.

examples.en: This year I plan to devote myself to studying.

examples.ko: 그는 연구에만 매진해서 좋은 결과를 냈어요.
examples.en: He focused only on research and got good results.

examples.ko: 시험 준비에 매진하느라 친구를 못 만났어요.
examples.en: I couldn't see friends because I was devoted to exam prep.
The athletes are fully committed to Olympic preparation.

examples.ko: 한 가지 일에 매진하면 실력이 늘어요.
examples.en: If you commit to one thing, your skills improve.
Tell me what you were dedicated to.

explain: '매진하다'는 한 가지 일에 온 힘을 쏟는다는 뜻이라 주로 '~에 매진하다'로 써요. '매진되다'(다 팔리다)와 소리는 같지만 뜻이 전혀 달라요. '열중하다'보다 격식 있고 목표를 향해 꾸준히 나아가는 느낌이 있어서 글과 인터뷰에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I will devote myself to studying until the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일에 온 힘을 쏟는다는 뜻으로 '~에 매진하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '~에 매진하다' pattern means putting all your effort into one thing.

phrases.en: He is devoting himself to his new business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목표를 향해 꾸준히 힘쓰는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a sense of steadily working toward a goal.

phrases.en: These days I'm absorbed in drawing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매진하다'보다 덜 격식 있고 푹 빠진 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less formal than '매진하다' and stresses being absorbed.

explain_en: Used as '~에 매진하다' (to pour all your effort into something). It sounds just like 매진되다 (sold out) but means something completely different. It is more formal than '열중하다' and carries a sense of steady progress toward a goal, common in writing and interviews.

examples.en: My father visited his alma mater last week for the first time in a long while.
I was so glad to meet a teacher from my old school.

examples.ko: 제 모교는 서울에 있는 작은 대학교예요.
examples.en: My alma mater is a small university in Seoul.
The graduates donated a scholarship fund to their alma mater.
I took photos with my friends in front of our old school.
I heard our alma mater won the national tournament!

explain: '출신 학교'는 사실을 말하는 느낌이고, 모교는 졸업한 학교를 정을 담아 부를 때 써요. 지금 다니는 학교에는 쓰지 않고, 주로 대학교나 고등학교를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I visited my alma mater for the first time since graduating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸업한 학교를 다시 찾아갈 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when returning to your old school.

phrases.en: I met a junior from my alma mater at work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 학교를 나온 아랫사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A younger person who attended the same school.

phrases.en: I got to give a talk at my alma mater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 붙여 장소로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle '에서' marks it as a location.

explain_en: '출신 학교' just states a fact, while 모교 calls your graduated school with some warmth. It is never used for the school you attend now, and it is most often said about a university or high school.

examples.en: The company is looking for a new way.

examples.ko: 문제를 해결할 방법을 함께 모색해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's look for a way to solve the problem together.
He explored starting a business instead of getting a job.
More people are seeking change.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 협력 방안을 모색하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two countries decided to explore ways to cooperate.
We need time to look for alternatives.

explain: '찾다'는 물건이나 사람에게도 쓰지만 '모색하다'는 해결 방법, 대안, 길처럼 아직 정해지지 않은 것을 찾을 때만 써요. 뉴스, 회의, 보고서에 자주 나오고 말투가 딱딱해요.

phrases.en: The government is seeking ways to support them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '방안'은 계획이나 방법이라는 뜻으로, 뉴스에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Bangan' means plan or method, and this is the pairing you hear most in the news.

phrases.en: We have to look for another alternative.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 방법이 안 될 때 다른 길을 찾는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means looking for another way when the current method does not work.

phrases.en: We are currently looking for a solution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 찾는 중이라는 진행의 뜻이고, 회의나 발표에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the search is still in progress, common in meetings and announcements.

explain_en: 찾다 works for objects and people, but 모색하다 is used only for things not yet settled, such as solutions, alternatives, or a path forward. It is a formal word common in news, meetings, and reports.

examples.en: My mother tongue is English, not Korean.

examples.ko: 모어로 말할 때는 감정을 더 잘 표현할 수 있어요.
examples.en: When you speak in your mother tongue, you can express feelings better.
Children learn their mother tongue naturally.

examples.ko: 외국에서 오래 살면 모어를 잊어버리기도 해요.
examples.en: If you live abroad for a long time, you sometimes forget your native language.

examples.ko: 모어가 다른 친구와 이야기하려고 한국어를 배워요.
examples.en: I'm learning Korean to talk with friends whose native languages differ from mine.

examples.ko: 모어 화자는 문법을 몰라도 자연스럽게 말해요.
examples.en: Native speakers speak naturally even without knowing the grammar.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '모국어'를 더 많이 쓰고, '모어'는 논문이나 언어 수업에서 자주 보여요. '모국어'는 내 나라의 말이라는 느낌이 있고, '모어'는 어릴 때 처음 배운 말을 가리켜요. 그래서 이민을 간 사람에게는 '모어'가 더 정확해요.

phrases.en: My native language is Vietnamese.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '모어'보다 '모국어'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation '모국어' is more common than '모어'.

phrases.example: 모어 화자와 이야기하면 발음이 많이 늘어요.
phrases.en: Talking with native speakers improves your pronunciation a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 언어를 모어로 하는 사람을 가리키는 말로 언어 수업에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person whose first language it is, often heard in language classes.

phrases.en: Korean is not my mother tongue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모어'에 '이/가 아니다'를 붙여 처음 배운 말이 아니라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a language is not the first one you learned.

explain_en: First language learned from birth; linguistics, formal (모어 화자) In daily talk 모국어 is used more, while 모어 shows up in papers and language classes. 모국어 carries the feel of 'my country's language', but 모어 means the language you first learned as a child. That makes 모어 more accurate for people who emigrated.

examples.en: I'll return to school next semester after the military.
My friend who took a leave finally returned to school this year.
Once I'm back at school, I'll start preparing to graduate.

examples.ko: 먼저 복학한 선배가 수업 정보를 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: A senior who returned earlier told me about the classes.
I plan to return to school after saving some money.

examples.ko: 복학하기 전에 수강 신청 방법을 확인했어요.
examples.en: Before returning to school, I checked how to register for courses.

explain: 복학하다는 쉬었던 학교로 돌아가는 일이고, 반대는 '휴학하다'예요. 한국에서는 군 복무 뒤에 복학하는 남학생이 많아서 이 이야기에 자주 나와요. 새로 들어가는 것은 '입학하다'라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: I'm planning to return to school next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으려고 하다'를 붙여 계획을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -(으)려고 하다 to talk about a plan.
phrases.en_equiv: to plan to return to school

phrases.example: 복학한 뒤에 공부를 열심히 할 거예요.
phrases.en: After I return to school, I'll study hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 뒤에'를 붙여 학교로 돌아온 다음 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -ㄴ 뒤에 to talk about what happens after returning.

phrases.en: There is an older student in my class who has returned to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬었다가 학교에 돌아온 학생을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a student who came back after taking time off.

explain_en: Returning to school, typically a student back after military service or leave. 복학하다 is going back to the school you had paused, and its opposite is 휴학하다. In Korea many male students return after military service, so the word comes up in that context a lot. Entering a school for the first time is 입학하다.

examples.en: A student's duty is to study.

examples.ko: 맡은 일을 열심히 하는 게 직원의 본분이에요.
examples.en: Doing your assigned work diligently is an employee's duty.
He fulfilled his duty as a doctor to the end.

examples.ko: 자기 본분을 잊고 놀기만 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't forget your duty and just play around.
Firefighters are faithful to their duty of saving people.

examples.ko: 자기 본분도 모르고 남의 일에 참견해요.
examples.en: He doesn't even know his own duty and meddles in other people's business.

explain: 사람이 자기 신분이나 역할에서 마땅히 해야 하는 일을 말해요. '학생의 본분'처럼 쓰고, '본분을 다하다·지키다·잊다'와 자주 어울려요. '의무'는 법이나 규칙이 정한 일에도 쓰는데, 본분은 역할에 맞는 도리라는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: A person who does their duty is admirable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맡은 역할을 끝까지 잘 해낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means fulfilling one's role to the end.

phrases.example: 바빠도 학생의 본분을 잊으면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: Even if you are busy, you must not forget your duty as a student.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잊으면 안 돼요'처럼 충고할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in advice such as 'you must not forget'.

phrases.en: If everyone sticks to their own duty, things go well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 역할에서 벗어나지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means not straying from one's own role.

explain_en: The basic duty fitting one's status (학생의 본분) It refers to what a person is supposed to do in their position or role. It is used as in '학생의 본분' and pairs often with '본분을 다하다·지키다·잊다'. '의무' can also cover things set by laws or rules, while '본분' feels more like the proper conduct of one's role.

t90.ax: A student's duty is to study.
